paragraphs.text: DSH plugin: enable permessage-deflate on the WebSocket transport (/api/remote.mux) without modifying
the DSH install tree
# dsh-ws-deflate
**English** | 简体中文
Turns on `permessage-deflate` for DeepSeek Harness (`dsh`) web's WebSocket transport, **without modi
fying the DSH installation**. Measured on one machine: a session transcript that left the server as
**1,206,822 B went out as 350,599 B — 70.9 % fewer wire bytes**.
It is a **runtime monkey-patch, not a supported extension point.** Read "Should I install this" befo
monkey-patch, not a supported extension point.** Read "Should I install this" before installing it.
## Should I install this?
**Install it if** you open `dsh web` from somewhere that is not your own machine — a Tailscale/VPN l
ink, a reverse proxy over the internet, any path with real latency or packet loss. DSH replays the w
hole session transcript over `/api/remote.mux` on every reconnect, so on a lossy link those bytes ar
cript over `/api/remote.mux` on every reconnect, so on a lossy link those bytes are paid repeatedly.
**Do not install it if** you only ever use `dsh web` on `localhost` or a LAN. The saving is real but
you don't need it there, and what you'd be taking on in exchange is a patch against another project
's internals that can go quietly stale on every upgrade.
What it costs, measured on a Windows 10 / node v24 box: **+10 ms** to `dsh` startup (alternating 4-r
un measurement), and zlib level 6 at **42.7 ms per 1.53 MB** of transcript. The compression is per-m
essage above a 1 KiB threshold, so small events are untouched.
## What it actually changes
Nothing on disk. `ws@8.22.0`, `@deepseek-ai/dsh-api-gateway`, and `@deepseek-ai/dsh/lib` were compar
ed file-by-file (sha256) against the pristine registry tarballs: **63 files, 0 mismatches, 0 extra,
0 missing**, and 0 files in the install tree written or created that day.
What it does change is one method, in memory, in the `dsh` process:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
The wrapper sets `this.options.perMessageDeflate` at **handshake** time, which works because ws 8.x
reads that option inside `handleUpgrade` (`websocket-server.js:299`/`:303`), not at construction — s
o it reaches the gateway's already-built `new WebSocketServer({ noServer: true })` (`dsh-api-gateway
/lib/index.js:179`). It only opts in when nothing else set the option, so **if DSH enables compressi
on itself upstream, this plugin steps aside automatically.**
Why the option can't just be configured: DSH exposes no key for it. The webserver's `compression` is
HTTP gzip and does not cover streams.
## Install
[代码示例省略，未执行]
Then restart `dsh web`. The bundle list is read at startup, so no restart means no effect.
## Verify
[代码示例省略，未执行]
You want three things:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
The **self test** is the interesting one. DSH's browser auth rejects non-browser handshakes, so you
cannot probe a live server from a script — the plugin instead builds its own `new WebSocketServer({
noServer: true })` on an ephemeral loopback port and does a real handshake against it. That proves *
this process, with this ws copy, negotiates*, which is the claim no external probe can reach. The `n
egotiated …` lines then log the first few real browser handshakes (user agent truncated, `maxLog` ca
ps it at 5, `0` disables).
Browser side, if you want it: DevTools → Network → the `remote.mux` request → Response Headers shoul
d contain `Sec-WebSocket-Extensions: permessage-deflate; …`.
## Uninstall
[代码示例省略，未执行]
Restart. Nothing needs restoring, because nothing on disk was ever different.
## Configuration
The entry **registers itself**. The bundle manifest points `dsh.bundle.patch` at the `cordis.patch.y
ml` shipped inside this package, and DSH inserts the entry while it composes the profile tree — your
own `cordis.patch.yml` never has to mention it. Proof, on this machine, from DSH itself:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
The entry carries no `config` block by design, so `--dump-config` shows only the id and the name. Th
e values actually in force are printed by the plugin at activation — the same line quoted under Veri
fy: `... (level 6, threshold 1024 B, noContextTakeover on)`. A `0.1.0` install still shows the seven
keys in its tree; they were dropped as duplication.
Override it only when you want non-default values, and use a **field-replacing patch, not an insert*
erride it only when you want non-default values, and use a **field-replacing patch, not an insert**:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
Two rules, both verified with `--dump-config` rather than taken on faith:
- **`insert` appends; it does not dedupe by id.** Copying the shipped patch into your profile file l
eaves **two** `- id: ws-deflate` entries in the tree — `level: 6` and `level: 1` both show up — so t

he override silently does nothing, or runs twice. Measured: entry count goes 1 -> 2.
- **`config` is
replaced wholesale, not deep-merged.** Any key you omit falls back to this plugin's schema defaults
, not to the bundle patch's values. So list every key you intend to keep.

| key | default | notes |
|---|---:|---|
| `enabled` | `true` | `false` keeps the wrapper installed

but opts no handshake in |
| `level` | `6` | measured here: level 6 → ratio 0.176, level 1 → 0.238 o

n the same payload, at 42.7 ms vs 5.9 ms per 1.53 MB |
| `thresholdBytes` | `1024` | below this, fra

mes go out raw (the median DSH event is ~800 B) |
| `noContextTakeover` | `true` | independent defla
te stream per frame: bounded memory, and a dropped frame cannot corrupt later messages. Costs ratio,

buys robustness on a lossy link — which is the whole reason to run this plugin |
| `concurrencyLimi

t` | `10` | cap on simultaneous compress operations |
| `selfTest` | `true` | run the loopback hands

hake at activation. Not hot-reloadable |
[该节后续省略]
## Security note
`permessage-deflate` is a compression feature and compression features have a BREACH-family history.
Here the protected secret and the attacker-controlled input are both inside your own session transc
ript, on a link you already trust to carry your token in a URL query string. If you are running `dsh
web` as plaintext HTTP on a public host, **fix that first** — it is a much bigger hole than anythin
g this plugin touches.
